sources.title: Virtualization & Microservice Architecture for Software-Defined Vehicles: An Evaluation and Exploration
sources.role: Author paper/preprint used to verify the reported architecture, method/evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The study evaluates KVM and several container technologies across embedded, AMD64 and ARM64 hardware using CPU, memory, network and disk benchmarks, then tests Autoware and k3s-based microservice decompositions.
The authors report roughly 0-5% CPU/memory/network performance decline versus bare metal in their generic tests, larger disk penalties, and platform-dependent effects for automotive workloads.
The authors find that Autoware start-up can improve under selected microservice decompositions, but the optimal container count is workload/platform specific rather than simply maximized.

metrics.name: generic CPU/memory/network performance decline
metrics.context: Reported range across tested virtualization/containerization environments versus bare metal.

metrics.name: KVM disk-performance loss
metrics.context: Reported maximum/representative loss versus bare metal in the paper's disk benchmark.

metrics.name: reported microservice start-up improvement
metrics.context: Best reported case relative to bare-metal Autoware on the tested AMD64 setup.

limitations.text: The paper shows different start-up behavior on AMD64 and ARM64, so the percentages are not portable across hardware/runtime configurations without retesting.
The authors explicitly find that the best microservice/container count is neither necessarily the maximum nor minimum and must be determined experimentally.
The study is a performance evaluation, not evidence that virtualization/containerization automatically satisfies automotive safety isolation, certification, or deterministic timing requirements.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Virtualization & Microservice Architecture for Software-Defined Vehicles: An Evaluation and Exploration; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The full primary paper verifies the multi-platform benchmark design, generic overhead ranges, Autoware experiments, microservice container-count trade-off, and reported start-up/disk effects.

editorial.why_now_note: This is unusually concrete measurement evidence for the virtualization/microservice layer that centralized SDV architectures increasingly depend on.
editorial.rationale: Strong candidate if all percentages stay attached to their tested platform/workload context rather than becoming generic virtualization claims.
